findings.location: Approach stage 3: 'Verifier directive: block only a defect-in-deliverable with NO recorded disposition; a filed+linked+reasoned deferral (accepted-with-reason, superseded-by, proven-pre-existing) SATISFIES'; AC line 'blocks only undispositioned deliverable-defects'.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace the invented tokens with a concrete, store-grounded rule: a disposition is SATISFIED when the bug carries (a) a supersedes/duplicates link to the epic or its replacement, OR (b) a reasoned comment/description asserting pre-existence, judged for substance by the verifier — and is NEVER satisfied by close_class alone. State that the verifier retrieves these via show_ticket, and map each regression fixture to the exact signal it uses.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the DET floor's coverage boundary explicitly (it fires only on caused_by edges present on open/in_progress bugs, which are hand-drawn since auto-derivation runs only at a bug's own close) and confirm the screen+verifier tier — not the floor — is the load-bearing net for the motivating 30a2/5b09 escapes.
evidence: Plan: 'any OPEN/IN_PROGRESS bug with caused_by -> epic or any descendant = deterministic block ... 0 historical FPs'
transition_close.py:493-525 `_apply_caused_by` runs on a BUG close; blame.py:100-102 `derive_caused_by` returns None without a fixing commit — an open/in_progress bug cannot be auto-derived
Real escapes 30a2/5b09 were bugs agents 'deem out-of-scope/pre-existing' — the population least likely to voluntarily draw a caused_by link to the epic
types.py:25 / ticket-model.md:120: caused_by is directional and set at bug close or by explicit link
findings.finding: The DET caused_by floor's effective coverage on the target population (agent-filed out-of-scope bugs) is near-zero, because a caused_by edge is auto-derived only on the BUG'S OWN close (requires a fixing commit), so an OPEN/IN_PROGRESS bug has a caused_by edge only when someone HAND-linked it — which the very agents who deem a bug out-of-scope are least likely to do. The floor's '0 historical FPs' is a precision claim, not a recall claim.
findings.location: Approach, stage 1 (DET floor); Context ('causation is the discriminator')
scenarios: An agent files a defect in the epic's deliverable, deems it out-of-scope, leaves it in_progress, and never draws a caused_by link — the DET floor sees nothing and the close proceeds to the (degrade-open) screen tier only.
Backtest 30a2/5b09 would have needed the SCREEN, not the floor, to catch them — implying the floor is not the load-bearing tier for the plan's own motivating cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line to the DET-floor rationale acknowledging that open-bug caused_by edges are operator-supplied (auto-derivation needs a fixing commit at bug close), so the floor is a high-precision backstop, not the primary recall mechanism; verify at least one regression must-block case (30a2 or 5b09) exercises the SCREEN path rather than only the floor, so the plan does not credit the floor with catches it cannot make.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that the must-pass fixtures (30d3, e6a0, c8ed) do NOT carry a caused_by edge into the subtree (they link via discovered_from / non-causal relations), so the DET floor cannot pre-empt the disposition-aware verifier path.
evidence: Stage 1: 'any OPEN/IN_PROGRESS bug with caused_by -> epic or any descendant = deterministic block'
DET floor unit test: 'discovered_from alone does not trip the floor'
Testing: '30d3-eaf0 ... e6a0-ba9b ... c8ed-d52d' listed as must-pass
findings.finding: Potential cross-section contradiction between the DET caused_by floor (Approach stage 1: any OPEN/IN_PROGRESS caused_by bug in the subtree = hard block, no verifier, only fix/re-parent/dispute) and the Testing must-pass set (30d3, e6a0, c8ed must PASS). If any must-pass fixture carries a caused_by edge into the subtree it would be blocked by the hard tier regardless of disposition. The plan should assert the must-pass fixtures link via discovered_from (or a non-caused_by relation), not caused_by.
findings.location: Approach stage 1 vs Testing (must-pass: 30d3-eaf0, e6a0-ba9b, c8ed-d52d)
scenarios: A legitimate deferral fixture that happens to carry a caused_by edge would be hard-blocked by stage 1, contradicting its must-pass status and defeating the disposition-aware SATISFIES path
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Testing note: each must-pass fixture's linkage relation is non-caused_by (discovered_from or similar), ensuring it flows to the screen/verifier rather than the hard floor.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py (the `completion_precheck` short-circuit) as an edit target for the DET floor, OR specify that the caused_by-floor findings are folded into `child_closure_findings`/`deterministic_child_failure` so the existing precheck block fires — the block is enforced there, not in completion.py.
evidence: gate_ops.py:62-74 — `blocking, uncertified = child_closure_findings(...)`; `if blocking:` returns `run_verify: False` + `deterministic_child_failure` (the short-circuit BLOCK lives HERE, not in completion.py)

completion.py:378-389 — production verdict runs through `gate_dispatch.produce_completion_verdict` -> the v3 workflow, whose `completion_precheck` op owns the deterministic precheck; completion.py itself does not enforce the block
Scope lists only completion.py + epic_bug_screen.py + completion_sidecar.py + docs + tests; gate_ops.py (outside completion.py) is unenumerated
findings.finding: The DET caused_by floor's ENFORCEMENT (short-circuit BLOCK) requires editing the workflow op `completion_precheck` in src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py, which the plan's Scope does not enumerate. The plan places the floor 'beside the direct-children gate, completion.py ~:90', but completion.py:89 `child_closure_findings` only COMPUTES findings; the actual block/no-LLM short-circuit is decided in gate_ops.py:completion_precheck (reads `blocking` -> `run_verify:False` + `deterministic_child_failure`). A new DET floor in completion.py that merely returns findings will not block a close unless its output is folded into `child_closure_findings`/`deterministic_child_failure` OR wired into completion_precheck.
findings.location: Scope: 'src/rebar/rebar/llm/completion.py (DET floor beside the direct-children gate...)'
scenarios: An open caused_by bug exists in the subtree; the floor helper is added to completion.py but completion_precheck is never taught to short-circuit on it -> the close is NOT blocked (AC1 unmet in practice).
findings.suggested_fix: Add gate_ops.py to Scope and state the wiring: extend `child_closure_findings` (or add a sibling helper) to surface open/in_progress caused_by bugs as `blocking` findings so `completion_precheck` already short-circuits, keeping exactly one enforcement point.
